subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Find the equations of the tangent and the normal to the curve y = x⁴ − 6x³ + 13x² − 10x + 5 at (0, 5).

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IB (2026-27 edition), book p.221, chapter 10 APPLICATIONS OF DERIVATIVES, the TANGENTS AND NORMALS sub-section, Short Answer question 10. recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say what you differentiate, what number you get for the slope at (0, 5), and how the normal's slope comes from it.

steps.label: Differentiate the curve
steps.margin_note: First mark. Write dy/dx in full before substituting anything. The one-line check that x = 0 gives y = 5 confirms the point is on the curve, and the examiner accepts it as part of the method.
lines: Check the point: at x = 0,  y = 0 − 0 + 0 − 0 + 5 = 5,
Differentiate term by term with respect to x:

recall.must_convey: That the curve is differentiated term by term to dy/dx = 4x³ − 18x² + 26x − 10.
accept: differentiate the polynomial term by term
dy by dx is four x cubed minus eighteen x squared plus twenty six x minus ten
bring each power down and reduce the index by one
prathi term ni differentiate cheyyali
the constant five differentiates to zero
first find dy by dx of the whole curve

steps.why: Both the tangent and the normal are built from the same derivative, so differentiating once is the whole starting move. A tangent can only be drawn at a point that lies on the curve, so the check at x = 0 is worth the one line it costs.
common_mistakes: Carrying the constant 5 into dy/dx instead of differentiating it to 0.
Reading the slope as 5 from the point (0, 5) instead of from the derivative.
steps.memory_tip: Differentiate the whole polynomial first, substitute second. A number put in early leaves nothing to differentiate.

steps.label: Slope of the tangent at (0, 5)
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Show the substitution line, not only the value. m = −10 must be a plain number before it can go into a line equation.
lines: The slope of the tangent is the value of dy/dx at the given point.

recall.must_convey: That putting x = 0 into dy/dx gives the tangent slope m = −10.
accept: substitute x equal to zero into dy by dx
the slope of the tangent is minus ten
every term with an x becomes zero so only minus ten is left
x equal to zero substitute cheste minus ten vasthundi
m is minus ten at this point
put the x of the point into the derivative

steps.why: dy/dx is a function of x, so it gives a different slope at every point. Only after x = 0 is substituted is m a fixed number that the line equation can use.
common_mistakes: Substituting y = 5 into dy/dx instead of x = 0.
Writing m = −10x and leaving x in the slope.
Substituting into the original curve instead of into dy/dx.
steps.memory_tip: At x = 0 every term carrying an x disappears, so the slope is just the constant term of dy/dx. Here that constant is −10.

steps.label: Equation of the tangent
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Quote y − y₁ = m(x − x₁) before substituting; the formula line itself carries part of the mark. Finish in the general form ax + by + c = 0.
lines: Tangent at (x₁, y₁) with slope m:   y − y₁ = m(x − x₁)

recall.must_convey: That the point-slope form with (0, 5) and m = −10 gives 10x + y − 5 = 0.
accept: use y minus y one equals m into x minus x one
y minus five equals minus ten x
the tangent is ten x plus y minus five equals zero
point slope form use chesi tangent rasta
substitute the point and the slope into the straight line formula
bring everything to one side for the general form

steps.why: The point-slope form is the shortest route from a point and a slope to an equation, and it needs no intercept. Moving every term to one side gives the standard form the board expects.
common_mistakes: Using the normal's slope 1/10 here instead of m = −10.
Leaving the answer as y = −10x + 5 when the general form is asked for.
steps.memory_tip: Point-slope form is y minus the y of the point, equals m times x minus the x of the point. Nothing else goes in.

steps.label: Equation of the normal
steps.margin_note: Fourth mark. The most common loss on this question is the normal's slope: it is −1/m, so −10 becomes +1/10, not −1/10. Check the answer by putting (0, 5) back in: 0 − 50 + 50 = 0.
lines: The normal is perpendicular to the tangent at the same point,

recall.must_convey: That the normal's slope is −1/m = 1/10, giving x − 10y + 50 = 0.
accept: the normal slope is minus one by m
minus ten turns into plus one over ten
the normal is x minus ten y plus fifty equals zero
normal slope ki minus one by m teesukovali
turn the slope upside down and change its sign
the normal passes through the same point five on the y axis

steps.why: The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so its slope is the negative reciprocal of m. Turning −10 into 1/10 needs both moves: the reciprocal and the sign change.
common_mistakes: Writing the normal's slope as −1/10, doing the reciprocal but not the sign change.
Using −m = 10 as the normal's slope instead of −1/m.
Writing the normal through a different point than (0, 5).
steps.memory_tip: Turn the tangent slope upside down, then change its sign. Both moves, every time.

insider_note: At x = 0 every power term vanishes, so m is just the coefficient of x, which is −10. That makes the normal slope 1/10.
